content: The references provided are a list of studies and articles related to the use, management, and complications of central venous catheters (CVCs), peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs), and peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVCs). 1. J Hosp Med, 2019: This study discusses the use of central venous catheters in hospital settings, focusing on their clinical applications and associated outcomes. 2. Kun C et al., Biomed Res (India), 2017: This research evaluates the impact of specialized training on nursing staff's knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding PICC insertion and catheter maintenance. 3. Larson E, Hargiss C, Am J Infect Control, 1984: The authors propose a decentralized approach to maintaining intravenous therapy, emphasizing infection control and improved outcomes. 4. Purran A et al., Nurs Standard, 2016: This study assesses the effectiveness of a PICC care training program in improving nursing practices and patient outcomes. 5. Romeo M et al., Ind J Public Health Res Develop, 2020: The authors examine the effectiveness of a comprehensive nurse-patient strategy in managing PIVCs and its impact on clinical outcomes. 6. Walters B, Price C, J Infus Nurs, 2019: This quality improvement initiative demonstrates a reduction in complications associated with PICCs through targeted interventions. 7. Zhang J et al., J Cent South Univ Med Sci, 2014: The study evaluates the effects of standardized PICC training and management on clinical outcomes and catheter-related complications. 8. Schults JA et al., PLoS One, 2022: This research explores the use of ultrasound guidance for PIVC insertion in patients with difficult venous access, providing insights into implementation strategies in Australian healthcare settings. 9. Marsh N et al., Trials, 2018: A pilot randomized controlled trial comparing the outcomes of PIVC insertions performed by expert versus generalist inserters. 10. Cooke M et al., PLoS One, 2018: This international survey highlights consumer perspectives on PIVC insertion, emphasizing the importance of patient-centered care. 11. Hirschmann H et al., J Hosp Infect, 2001: The study investigates the influence of hand hygiene prior to PIVC insertion on the frequency of complications. 12. Kaufman DA et al., JAMA Pediatr, 2014: A randomized clinical trial examining the use of nonsterile gloves in addition to hand hygiene to prevent late-onset infections in preterm infants. 13. Penney-Timmons E, J Assoc Vasc Access, 2005: This article discusses the cost-effectiveness and improved outcomes associated with standardized intravenous equipment. 14. Adhikari S et al., J Ultrasound Med, 2010: A comparison of infection rates between ultrasound-guided and traditionally placed peripheral intravenous lines. 15. Avelar AF et al., J Infus Nurs, 2015: A randomized controlled trial evaluating ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous access in children. 16. Barber JM et al., Clin Radiol, 2002: This study highlights the effectiveness of a nurse-led PICC insertion service supported by radiological guidance. 17. Bauman M et al., Am J Emerg Med, 2009: A comparison of ultrasound-guided versus standard techniques for vascular access in patients with difficult venous access. 18. Bridey C et al., BMJ Open, 2018: A randomized controlled study comparing ultrasound-guided and landmark approaches for PIVC insertion by critical care nurses. 19. Chen MH et al., Europ J Cancer Care, 2017: The application of PICCs in acute myeloid leukemia patients undergoing induction chemotherapy is analyzed. 20. Desai K et al., J Assoc Vasc Access, 2018: This study compares the longevity and complication rates of ultrasound-guided versus traditional PIVCs in pediatric emergency departments. 21. Gong P et al., Asian Pac J Cancer Preven, 2012: A comparison of complications associated with PICCs placed using ultrasound guidance versus conventional methods in cancer patients. 22. Hanada S et al., Anaesthesia, 2017: A randomized study comparing dynamic ultrasound-guided needle tip navigation with the landmark technique for saphenous vein access in children. 23. Li J et al., Europ J Oncol Nurs, 2014: A randomized controlled trial comparing long-term outcomes of PICC placement using B-mode ultrasound with the modified Seldinger technique versus blind puncture. 24. McCarthy ML et al., Ann Emerg Med, 2016: A randomized controlled trial comparing ultrasound-guided versus landmark techniques for PIVC cannulation. 25. Qi YZ et al., Chin J Clin Nutr, 2012: A study comparing PICC placement using vascular ultrasound guidance systems and traditional methods in tumor patients. 26. Rodriguez-Herrera A et al., Healthcare, 2022: The use of ultrasound guidance is compared to standard techniques for improving venous cannulation in patients with difficult access. 27. Sengul T, Acaroğlu R, J Educ Res Nurs: This study evaluates the effectiveness of ultrasound in PIVC application. 28. Stokowski G et al., J Infus Nurs, 2009: The use of ultrasound to improve practice and reduce complication rates in PICC insertions is discussed. 29. Tan J et al., Springerplus, 2016: A cost-effectiveness analysis of ultrasound-guided Seldinger PICC placement is presented. 30. Tang H et al., Chin J Clin Nutr, 2012: The combination of vascular ultrasound and Seldinger technology is shown to improve PICC success rates and reduce complications. 31. Wang Q et al., Pak J Med Sci, 2016: The clinical effects of PICCs placed using the modified Seldinger technique under vascular ultrasound guidance are analyzed. 32. Yin T et al., Dis Markers, 2022: A retrospective study on the application value of ultrasound-guided technology in neonatal peripheral deep venous catheterization. 33. Yuan L et al., J Assoc Vasc Access, 2013: The effects of three PICC insertion techniques in Chinese patients with varying vascular statuses are compared. 34. Zhang L et al., Anti-Tumor Pharm, 2019: The application of PICC catheterization using the modified Seldinger technique under B-mode ultrasound guidance in chemotherapy patients is discussed. 35. Weiner SG et al., J Emerg Med, 2013: Single-operator ultrasound-guided intravenous line placement by emergency nurses reduces the need for physician intervention in patients with difficult IV access. 36. Stein J et al., Ann Emerg Med, 2009: A randomized trial of ultrasound-guided PIVC cannulation in emergency department patients with difficult IV access. 37. Constantino TG et al., Ann Emerg Med, 2005: A comparison of ultrasound-guided PIVC access versus traditional approaches in patients with difficult IV access. 38. Ni Chronin D et al., Australas J Ageing, 2023: A national cross-sectional study on the burden of PIVCs in older hospital inpatients. 39. De Paula Magerote N et al., Texto Contexto Enferm, 2011: The association between phlebitis and the removal of PIVCs is analyzed. 40. DeVries M, Strimbu K, J Infus Nurs, 2019: The performance of short PIVCs following the adoption of clinical indication removal is evaluated. 41. Kagel EM, Rayan GM, J Trauma, 2004: Complications of intravenous catheters in the hand and forearm are discussed. 42. Kishihara Y et al., Front Med, 2022: A study of risk factors for phlebitis in ICU patients stratified by the APACHE II score. 43. Murayama R et al., Drug Discov Ther, 2018: The causes of PIVC failure based on the shape of removed catheters are explored. 45. Wallis MC et al., Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol, 2014: Risk factors for PIVC failure are analyzed using multivariate data from a randomized controlled trial. 47.
